reason: At base the JIT fastpass keeps the value written alongside a swallowed issue, so safeParse({}) succeeds but data contains the leaked key a, violating the expected no-key result.

After the fix the JIT branch guards the value assignment on !issues.length || present, so an absent optional key with a failing check is dropped and a present failing key reports failure, matching the PR test.
Before the fix the paragraph continuation lookahead only treated spaces-only lines as blank, so a tab-only separator line is absorbed as lazy continuation and only one paragraph is produced.
The widened [ \t]+\n lookahead now treats a tab-only line as blank, so the two text lines render as two separate paragraphs as expected.
A successful 200 response with application/json body is parsed to an object by default in axios; the PR only touches error-path stack decoration, so this behaviour is unchanged at base.
The PR only changes error stack decoration and leaves the success path untouched, so default JSON parsing of a 200 response still yields an object.
Parsing a plain boolean flag like --verbose is core commander behaviour unrelated to the negative-number regex change, so it works at base.
The regex change only affects negative-number argument detection; a simple boolean flag still parses as true after the PR.
Before the PR the tree-based JsonTreeReader.nextInt goes straight to getAsInt with no ASCII validation, so full-width digits are silently coerced to 123 instead of raising a parsing error.
After the PR nextInt validates string tokens with validateAscii and throws MalformedJsonException mentioning non-ASCII, matching the expected error for full-width digits.
The old allowlist regex splits test-db on the hyphen, issuing set search_path to two schemas instead of the single quoted schema name.
The new blocklist regex keeps hyphenated and accented names intact, so search_path is set to the single schema test-db as expected.
Applying a center-crop transformation by default is standard Glide behaviour; the ByteBufferUtil buffer-leak fix does not touch transformation eligibility.
The resource-leak fix only adds try/finally buffer recycling in ByteBufferUtil; default transformation behaviour on ImageView loads is unaffected.
allowed_symbols handling already works at base since the union CharacterSet is computed on demand for every checked name.
The caching refactor refreshes the union when allowedSymbols is set, preserving the same accept-an-allowed-symbol behaviour as the computed property.
Node-canvas percent-decodes non-base64 data URI payloads when loading images, and the GCC 15 include fix does not affect that behaviour at base.

Arrow shift applies timedelta to a tz-stripped datetime and re-localizes, yielding wall-clock arithmetic (04:30 CDT) rather than the expected absolute 10-hour result 05:30 with -05:00 offset; the Afrikaans locale PR is unrelated.
Node-canvas already percent-decodes non-base64 data URI payloads before parsing, and the GCC 15 include fix does not change image loading behaviour.
Vapor urlencoded-form decoding of an empty body yields an empty structure that satisfies an all-optional Decodable type, and the cookie-parsing PR does not touch content decoding at base.
The multi-cookie-header fix only changes HTTPCookies parsing; empty urlencoded bodies still decode to an all-nil optional struct at head.
Afero MemMapFs.Remove rejects a directory containing files with a not-empty error, matching OS semantics; the spelling-only PR does not affect this at base.
The comment and test-variable spelling fixes leave MemMapFs.Remove behaviour unchanged, so removing a non-empty directory still errors and keeps the contents.

Doctrine DBAL at this revision still raises an undefined array key PHP warning in detectIndexRenamings when two added indexes both match one removed index; the json_encode test-flag fix does not address the comparator.
The test-only json_encode flag fix leaves the comparator untouched, so the undefined array key warning on two equally valid index renames still occurs at head.

Arrow shift performs wall-clock arithmetic via a tz-stripped datetime plus timedelta, giving 04:30 CDT rather than the expected absolute-time result 05:30 at -05:00; the Afrikaans locale PR is unrelated.

Lowering the limit below available permits makes the scheduled refresh release a negative permit count, throwing and permanently suppressing further refresh executions, so admissions stop; the circuit breaker predicate fix is unrelated.
The circuit breaker predicate-leak fix does not touch the rate limiter, so lowering the limit below available permits still kills the scheduled refresh task and admissions stop permanently.

The no-var autofixer refuses to rewrite a var that is referenced before its declaration (the scope is marked unstable), so the file keeps var semantics and prints undefined; the prefer-template ASI PR is unrelated.
Indirect use-before-declaration still marks the var scope unstable so no-var leaves the declaration unmodified at head, and the prefer-template change does not affect that rule.
Scrapy JOBDIR persistence replays the saved scheduler queue and filters re-seen sitemap URLs, so a SitemapSpider resumes remaining pages; the log adapter fix is unrelated at base.
Resuming with the same JOBDIR continues crawling persisted pending requests regardless of the logformatter_adapter change, so the resumed run crawls more than zero pages.
At this revision bat still underflows/capacity-panics when a double-width character exceeds a terminal width of 1 under highlight-line, and the sanitize bidi fix does not touch the wrapping code.
Row-background themes still panic rendering double-width characters at terminal width 1; the bidi sanitize change only affects preprocessor substitution, not width math.
Fluentd writes buffered chunks one per write call with per-chunk metadata, so both key symlinks are created; the syslog regexp optimization does not touch file output at base.
Follow-up records for a seen key update that key symlink through normal per-chunk processing, unaffected by the RFC5424 regexp change.

Pool construction does not hold the JVM-wide system properties lock (plain System.getProperty reads are brief and the naming counter is atomic), and the virtual-thread ConcurrentBag change is unrelated.

Concurrent unnamed pool creation uses an atomic counter and short property reads, so no deadlock with unrelated system-property holders; the yield-spin change is in ConcurrentBag handoff, not initialization.
32-bit Redis 6.2 supports multi-megabyte BGSAVE (long CI-covered configuration), and the ACL key-check fix does not touch the persistence path.
Automatic save points trigger a normal successful background save on 32-bit builds under systemd; the SORT ACL parser fix is unrelated to RDB persistence.
CTRL-A parses the number into a 64-bit varnumber and a 50-digit value overflows it, so leading digits are truncated rather than preserved; the CWD context PR does not change this.
CTRL-X has the same 64-bit varnumber limit, so decrementing a 50-digit number loses leading digits instead of preserving all of them at head.
DuckDB binds the untyped NULL to the list operand type, so [1] || NULL yields a NULL of INTEGER[] rather than a scalar type; the file cache race fix is unrelated to binding.
The || list overload and list_concat share the same binding of untyped NULLs to list type, so both typeof calls report INTEGER[] and agree at head.
Godot emits NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE from Object destruction before memory is freed, so the RefCounted instance is still valid and members are readable; the scrollbar input change is unrelated.
Releasing the last reference still fires the PREDELETE notification while the object is intact, printing the stored data without crashing at head.
f_regression defaults to force_finite=True and computes under np.errstate, so a constant column yields F=0.0, p=1.0 with no RuntimeWarning; the tree criterion change is unrelated.

r_regression computes correlations under np.errstate with finite fallback, returning a finite value for a low-variance column without warnings; the decision-tree ValueError change does not touch feature selection.
Vault Agent file sink honors the configured octal mode when writing the token file, and the swagger UI readonly fix does not affect agent sinks.
The file sink applies mode 0600 to the token output at head; the UI-only change leaves sink permissions untouched.
Click appends the default [OPTIONS] metavar to the usage line even for a command with no parameters, so the first line is Usage: cli [OPTIONS], not Usage: cli.
The write_usage fix only affects rendering when args is empty; the [OPTIONS] metavar is still collected for a parameterless command, so the usage line remains Usage: cli [OPTIONS].
Flask jsonify converts returned dicts to compact JSON with application/json content type by default; the IPv6 partition fix in the dev server and test client is unrelated.
Flask automatically jsonifies returned dicts with compact separators and application/json content type; the IPv6 host parsing fix does not touch response serialization.
Omitting a required field always raises a pydantic ValidationError identifying the missing field; the unhashable generic alias fix only affects schema generation for exotic annotations.
Required-field validation is core pydantic behaviour and unaffected by the deprecated-typing-alias lookup change.
SQLAlchemy defaults the sqlalchemy logger to WARNING level so echo-off INFO SQL records are suppressed, and WARN and WARNING are the same numeric level at base.
Renaming the constant to logging.WARNING leaves the level value and default suppression behaviour unchanged, so echo-off captures nothing and echo-on logs SQL.
The aliased select attribute gets a generated reader defined on first access, so tens of thousands of subsequent reads dispatch to a real method at column-like cost.
The thread-safe lazy definition still generates the alias accessor on first access, keeping repeated computed-attribute reads close to real column access cost at head.
At base each dispatch stores a fresh WrappedListener in the callStack and called listeners are never removed, so two dispatches yield two getCalledListeners entries as expected.
After the leak fix the called-listener list is deduplicated per original listener and event, so the second invocation of the same listener is not reported again and the count is one, not two.
The legacy bash completion script scopes custom completion functions per subcommand via the last_command dispatch, and the shellcheck COMPREPLY rewrite is functionally equivalent for word lists.
Appending compgen results instead of word-splitting preserves the per-subcommand custom function dispatch, so each sibling subcommand still gets its own dynamic suggestions at head.
qs 6.13.0 applies the default arrayLimit of 20, so a key repeated 25 times is combined into a numerically-keyed object rather than an array.
qs 6.14.0 stops converting repeated-key results into an indexed object, so 25 repeated ids values parse as a 25-element array at head.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only the url parameter and returns the environment proxy dict without error when called with a single argument.
After the PR get_environ_proxies requires a second positional no_proxy argument, so calling it with only a URL raises a TypeError.
A bare word starting with a dot is not a numeric literal and parse_unit_value rejects it at base, so [.foons] parses as a string list and get 0 returns .foons.
Even with leading-dot acceptance in parse_unit_value, .foons has no valid numeric part or unit suffix, so it still falls back to a bare string at head.
At base Guzzle connects a sink write callback for HEAD requests, and with Accept-Encoding set the curl transfer aborts with a fatal write error instead of completing.
After the fix no sink or write callback is registered for HEAD requests, so the curl transfer with Accept-Encoding completes and returns a valid response.
The match failure between an atom and a map falls back to plain inspection in the diff formatter, and Inspect renders the improper list fine, so the assertion fails cleanly at base.
The map-in-list escape change does not affect inspection of an improper list value in a match failure, so the standard match error is still produced without a formatting crash.
At base the css_props teardown removes the wrapped element and dynamic component hydration is broken, so the custom property is lost after toggling the dynamic component.
The PR removes the element-removing teardown and routes dynamic components through the same component/css_props path, keeping the CSS custom property applied across re-renders.

At base the transform runs whenever the code contains new URL and import.meta.url, and the handling regex uses \s* which matches across newlines, so a multi-line reference is still emitted as a static asset.
After the refactor the hook filter /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ does not match across newlines, so the transform is skipped for multi-line calls and the asset is not bundled at head.
At base fzf exports no item-derived environment variable, so a NUL byte in the current item cannot break execve and the preview command runs normally.
After the change FZF_CURRENT_ITEM is built from the raw item text, and a NUL byte in an environment variable makes execve fail so the preview child process never starts.
At base switching to edge-to-edge replaces the decor system-ui visibility with layout-only flags, clearing the immersive sticky hide bits so the bars reappear.
After the change the edge-to-edge branch only calls WindowCompat and returns without clearing the immersive sticky hide flags left by setSystemUiVisibility, so the bars stay hidden after the switch.
At base ruff has no multiple-assignment check for case patterns, so the valid keyword-name-equals-capture pattern produces no diagnostics.

The new visitor inserts the keyword attribute name into the seen set before visiting its pattern, so ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) falsely reports multiple assignments to num_classes as a syntax error.
At base the decoder indexes the destination slice without growing it, so decoding two blocks into a one-element value slice panics with index out of range.
After the fix the slice is grown via reflect.Append before indexing, so two blocks decode into the pre-populated list without panic, overwriting the placeholder.
At base the mock keeps the timezone of the mocked moment when no timezone is requested, so now() is presented in America/Los_Angeles rather than the UTC default.
After the change the mocked instance is converted to the application default timezone when none is pinned, so now() formats as the reference moment in UTC.

The old protocol-relative regex requires exactly two consecutive slashes followed by a non-slash, so three leading slashes, tab-separated slashes, and slash-backslash forms are not classified as protocol-relative.
The widened regex ^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\] matches three leading slashes, tab-separated slashes, and slash-backslash forms, classifying all three as protocol-relative at head.
Guava MD5 hashing of the UTF-8 string abc produces the standard digest 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72; the combineOrdered accessor change does not affect md5().
The internal-accessor micro-optimization changes no hash values, so md5 of abc still yields the expected lowercase hex digest at head.
The source generator produces the same stub client for a properly attributed interface at base; only the diagnostic descriptor definitions were relocated.
Moving diagnostic descriptors to a dedicated class leaves codes and messages unchanged, so generation and the emitted GET request behave identically at head.
A simple HTTP/1.1 GET with Content-Length body is core hyper behaviour; removing only redundant trailing continue statements does not alter control flow at base.
The removed continues were loop-terminal no-ops, so HTTP/1.1 request/response framing and body reading are unchanged at head.
At base to_iso8601/2 converts the date to the ISO calendar then calls to_iso8601/1, dropping the requested :basic format and returning the extended string instead.
After the fix to_iso8601/2 forwards the requested format through the ISO conversion, so the Holocene date returns 2001-01-01 extended and 20010101 basic as expected.
On PHP 8.2+ the native end property is engine-managed and never re-synced at base, so after setEndDate the end property still reports the original 2024-09-30 value.
syncNativePeriod reinitializes the parent DatePeriod after end-date updates, so both the end property and getEndDate report 2025-06-15 at head.
At base the client builds the request line from whatever the normalizer returned and sends the embedded newline without raising an error.
After the change the headline builder rejects any whitespace in the resolved request URI, raising RequestError before transmission for a path containing a newline.
English number-to-words already renders 1000000 as one million and 2000000 as two million; the Albanian locale data change does not affect the default English output.
The Albanian pluralName data change leaves the default English formatter untouched, so one million and two million render correctly at head.
Singleton scope resolution returning the same instance is core Koin behaviour, unaffected by the property-loading ClassCastException fix at base.
The Properties filtering change does not touch instance resolution, so two resolutions of a singleton still yield the identical object at head.
replaceElement(at:withKey:value:) already appends, swaps into position, removes the old element and guards duplicate keys with a precondition, so the described behaviour holds at base.
The shared _replaceNew primitive performs the identical append-swap-remove steps and keeps the duplicate-key precondition, preserving the behaviour at head.
parseSizeInBytes clamps the negative parsed value to zero with the manual check at base, so -5MB yields 0 bytes.
The built-in max(cast.ToInt, 0) is equivalent to the manual negative clamp, so -5MB still returns zero at head.

At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec treats children[0] as the wildcard child, so with a static child plus :id param the unmatched-path lookup panics with invalid node type instead of returning not found.
After the fix static children are tried via indices and the wildcard is taken from the end, so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to the static route and /prefix/a/b/c returns not found without panicking.
At base Int64Value dereferences the nil big.Int through toBigInt and panics, while Float64Value returns zero, so the consistency check cannot pass.
The toBigInt nil guard makes a valid-but-empty Numeric report zero for both Float64Value and Int64Value without any runtime error at head.
External Quit from another goroutine terminates the event loop and Run returns; the renderer tab-stop fix does not affect shutdown handling at base.
Tab-stop setup changes only affect rendering, so the run loop still returns promptly after an external quit at head.
At base RunUntilCancelledFuture polls the wrapped future before checking cancellation, so the panicking inner operation is started even though the token is already cancelled.
After the fix run_until_cancelled checks is_cancelled before the future is ever polled, returning Ready(None) immediately without starting the inner operation.

Case-insensitive matching is handled by the grep matcher, not the directory walker, so all occurrences of the term are found regardless of case at base; the ignore-file skipping optimization is unrelated.
The walker change only skips loading ignore files for unreachable directories and does not affect case-insensitive pattern matching, so all cased variants still match at head.
A field with skip_deserializing and no custom default is initialized to Default::default() by the derived Deserialize at base, so the omitted field holds zero.
The nesting-removal refactor keeps the same condition, so skipped fields still receive their type default when absent from the input at head.
